question: Who among the following was the 24th Tirthankara in Jainism, in ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vardhamana Mahavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Vardhamana Mahavira

 
 
• Vardhamana Mahavira was born at Kundgrama near Vaishali in Bihar.
 
• His father, Siddharth was the head of the "Jantrika clan" of Kshatriyas.
 
• His mother, Trishala belonged to the Lichchhavi tribe.
 
• After getting true knowledge, he came to be known as the master of "Kevalajana".
 
• He was the 24th Tirthankara of the Jain religion.
 
• He died at Pawapuri in Bihar.
 
• The lion is a symbol of Mahavir.
 
• His discipline was known as Chandrabala.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Vasupujya

 
 
• Vasupujya was the twelfth Tirthankara of Jainism.
 
• According to Jain beliefs, he became a siddha, a liberated soul which has destroyed all of its karma.
 
• He attained moksha at Champapuri, Bhagalpur in India on the fourteenth day of the bright half of the month of Ashadh.
 
 
 
• Rishabhanatha
 
 
• Rishabhanatha was the first Tīrthaṅkara of Jainism.
 
• In paintings of the Shvetambara (“White-Robed”) sect, he is always gold in colour; in paintings of the Digambara (“Sky-Clad,” i.e., naked) sect, he is yellow.
 
• His symbol is the bull.
 
• His death is believed to have occurred on Ashtapada (also known as Mount Kailash) on the fourteenth day of Magha Krishna (Hindu Calendar).**​**
